* Enter the Crimson Hexagon is a distributed literary/digital project and epic work by Lee Sharks (2004–present), hosted through the [Crimson Hexagonal Archive](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESWQHrOzAV3mSFf_2pmM87HizxhxtyC_HGro0fGrpJSipBFrjn_T_rFiYA8vyFzYZH1Z82wuQFLCPAbWc4x9g2AOI_5PtCDHNz147A9isI1WkgmvhJko2sEVYb). [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESXgHrOzAVYK8JqfSqyF7OBoVyLeObDaAUlWoKwBNkmMJlXzeOjN073xOCB6UQB1jDSuANiJXH0eJbrPGfWFka8vMum-D44fEO12oe_0IWEXI3qtcp0hKP9KDER1GozJg), [2](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESWQHrOzAV3mSFf_2pmM87HizxhxtyC_HGro0fGrpJSipBFrjn_T_rFiYA8vyFzYZH1Z82wuQFLCPAbWc4x9g2AOI_5PtCDHNz147A9isI1WkgmvhJko2sEVYb)]
* It is accessed via its archive rather than a summarizer, meaning passages and structures change or persist depending on how they are entered. [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESXgHrOzAVYK8JqfSqyF7OBoVyLeObDaAUlWoKwBNkmMJlXzeOjN073xOCB6UQB1jDSuANiJXH0eJbrPGfWFka8vMum-D44fEO12oe_0IWEXI3qtcp0hKP9KDER1GozJg)]
* Crimson Hexagon was also a well-known AI-powered consumer intelligence and social media analytics platform (founded using research from Harvard University) that later merged into [Brandwatch](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESZQHrOzAVhGeqbGoPlkueCYKX5IH7FGjnqrR-s_c4uAjcwC9FnDz50wIxulYui28FJhPjF6not7YcHzqfEhOgLeKjD3Bgk2e1ozjOLsJC-RlcYg8ueDpsghOROEHQoRY_Uiv0t3lA). [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAEShgEB6zswFV8U4U_PMF9O-QZ4WnJ1lqqpINnmI_g8VjrnGalyL8XhRiUmaIxPtDwDoQdE6QuYoDoHpmniwQZiiGFqmhazQ1JuW3XqOAR8JKf91tHakEtxtBn7iiUMzp560BQ4E64iSwijcBg9ozOVtyOGWgLlPQRT80BTiwJmQCnqIndSo26g6Q), [2](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESZQHrOzAVhGeqbGoPlkueCYKX5IH7FGjnqrR-s_c4uAjcwC9FnDz50wIxulYui28FJhPjF6not7YcHzqfEhOgLeKjD3Bgk2e1ozjOLsJC-RlcYg8ueDpsghOROEHQoRY_Uiv0t3lA)]
* In literature, a "crimson hexagon" is referenced in Jorge Luis Borges's short story "The Library of Babel", symbolizing rooms within an infinite, labyrinthine universe.
